key_insight: RNADyn introduces a standardized benchmark for RNA dynamics, making it possible to fairly evaluate models that both generate RNA trajectories and understand how RNA moves over time. It fills a major data and evaluation gap by pairing high-quality MD simulations with leakage-controlled splits.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of large-scale, standardized RNA dynamics data and the common practice of evaluating trajectory generation and dynamics understanding as separate tasks. It also tackles data leakage issues that can inflate performance estimates.
method: Curates RNADynBench: 2,585 quality-controlled 100-ns all-atom RNA molecular dynamics trajectories.
Uses leakage-controlled dataset splits to ensure realistic generalization testing.
Provides a benchmark that unifies generation and understanding of RNA dynamics within one evaluation framework.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark offers a reliable way to compare models on RNA dynamics without hidden data leakage. It can accelerate progress on biologically meaningful generative models and better dynamics-aware representation learning.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing RNA structure -> molecular dynamics simulation -> benchmark dataset -> model evaluation.

Leaderboard-style chart or radar plot for generation and understanding metrics.
paper_title: RNADyn: A Benchmark for Generating and Understanding RNA Dynamics
paper_authors: Yiming Huang, Lennart Bastian, Hanqun Cao, Luis Vollmers, Tolga Birdal
